T: Santa needs a Mrs. And a menu.
D: Scott Calvin has to find a Mrs. Claus before Christmas Eve or stop being Santa for good.
P: Serve the cocoa when Scott takes Carol on their first date.
S: the elves' workshop at the North Pole
Iced Christmas sugar cookies cut into stars and trees, the kind the elves keep piled up all over the workshop.
A herby cheese ball rolled in walnuts and parsley with crackers, for the staff party Scott turns magical.
M: Golden roast chicken with herbs, potatoes and carrots, a warm Christmas dinner fit for the future Mrs. Claus.
W: Toy Santa running the North Pole
Fudgy chocolate brownies topped with crushed candy canes, sweet enough for a sugar-crazed toy Santa.
K: the elves' famous North Pole cocoa
Rich hot chocolate with whipped cream and a candy cane to stir.

s.note: the elves' workshop at the North Pole
s.how: Beat 200g butter and 100g icing sugar, add 1 egg yolk and 300g plain flour and chill. Roll out, cut stars and trees and bake at 170C for 12 minutes. Ice with 250g icing sugar tinted red and green.
Mix 250g cream cheese with 100g grated cheddar and a handful of snipped chives. Shape into a ball, roll in 50g chopped walnuts and parsley and chill. Serve with 200g crackers.

m.how: Rub a whole chicken with 40g butter and thyme and roast at 200C for 1 hour 15 minutes. Add 800g halved potatoes and 3 carrots to the tray for the last 50 minutes and rest before carving.

w.note: Toy Santa running the North Pole
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 180g butter, beat in 300g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour and 30g cocoa. Bake at 170C for 28 minutes, cool and scatter with 4 crushed candy canes.

d.note: the elves' famous North Pole cocoa
d.how: Heat 1L milk until steaming, whisk in 150g chopped dark chocolate and 2 tbsp sugar until smooth. Pour into 4 mugs, top with whipped cream and hang a candy cane on each.
